title: Service Commitments activation campaign — cross-team plan
body:
Purpose and framing:
- Goal: launch a coordinated activation campaign that helps product and infra teams adopt formal service commitments (latency/availability/error thresholds), operational runbooks, and a lightweight measurement pipeline. We deliberately use the term 'service commitments' to highlight product-facing promises while retaining SLO-like measurement internally.

Scope (what this campaign covers):
- Pilot with 3 services representing different risk profiles: hosted-api (high traffic), model-queue (batch/throughput), and console (admin UIs).
- Deliverables: agreements (commitment spec per service), automated telemetry dashboards, runbooks + alert routing, a cross-team oncall rotation proposal, and a customer-facing FAQ draft.
- Out of scope: full org-wide SLA pricing/legal contractization (this campaign will hand off to GTM/legal once internal commitments are stable).

Success metrics (campaign-level):
- 3 pilot services have formal commitment specs and dashboards within 8 weeks.
- Reduction in incident-to-detection median by 30% for pilot services.
- Runbook coverage: >= 90% of critical error modes documented and validated in playbook drills.
- Product leads sign off on customer-facing commitment statements for the pilots.

High-level timeline (8-week campaign):
- Week 0 (prep): kickoff, inventory of candidate services, identify owners, baseline telemetry snapshot.
- Weeks 1–2: commitment design workshops (measurement definition, error budgets mapped to product consequences).
- Weeks 3–4: implement dashboards and alert rules; assemble runbook drafts; test synthetic monitors.
- Week 5: runbook tabletop + 1-hour war room rehearsal with SRE/feature team/SEs.
- Week 6: iterate on metrics and alert tuning; finalize oncall rota proposals.
- Week 7: customer-facing copy review with Product & Legal; internal trainings for support and SEs.
- Week 8: go/no-go review and launch for pilots; retro and scale plan.

Roles & owners (single-string assignments):
- Campaign lead: Priya Natarajan (eng-sre) — overall coordination, success metric tracking.
- Product partner: Emma Chen (product-hosted-api) — product tradeoffs and customer messaging.
- Platform telemetry: Marcus Li (platform-engineering) — dashboard templates, query authorship.
- Runbook authoring: Ava Rodriguez (serving-runtime) — playbook drafts and rehearsal lead.
- Support liaison: Liam O'Neill (customer-success) — support playbooks and FAQ input.

Cross-functional touchpoints (meeting rhythm):
- Weekly 45-minute sync (Tues 10am) — status, blockers, decisions.
- Biweekly design workshop (Thurs 2pm) — measurement & alert design deep dive.
- Runbook rehearsal (Week 5) — 60–90 minutes, recorded, with action log.

Key templates and artifacts to produce:
- Commitment spec template: metric name, target window, target value, importance (customer impact), acceptable mitigation.
- Runbook template: detection signal, impact assessment, immediate mitigations, escalation path, roll-forward/rollback actions.
- Dashboard template: golden metrics, error budget burn, latency percentiles, alert counts.
- Communication checklist: internal comms, support playbook sync, and external copy for docs/faq.

Dependencies and blockers:
- Observability gaps: some services lack 99th percentile latency dashboards or per-route error counts — platform team to prioritize.
- Alert duplication: avoid spurious noise during tuning; need temporary suppression policy during rollout.
- Legal review timeline: customer-facing commitment language may require 2-week legal turnaround.

Risk log (top entries):
- Risk: Premature public commitments causing customer confusion. Mitigation: internal-only commitments until product signoff; staged external messaging.
- Risk: Alert storm during tuning leading to fatigue. Mitigation: synthetic-mode toggles and temporary silencing windows; pre-runbook drill to validate.
- Risk: Incomplete telemetry -> incorrect burn calculations. Mitigation: conservative default thresholds and manual overrides until telemetry coverage verified.

Tactical decisions required (for steering committee):
- Decision: definition of "critical" vs "major" incident thresholds for product teams.
- Decision: whether error-budget burn triggers automated capacity reallocation or only human review for pilots.

Communication plan (audiences & channels):
- Internal exec brief (week 2): 1-page slide for CTO & VP eng summarizing pilot selection and risk.
- Feature teams: weekly syncs + runbook workshop invites; link to living doc on Confluence.
- Support & SEs: walkthrough session (week 7) and annotated FAQ.
- Customers (post-pilot): staged blog + support docs, coordinated with legal & marketing.

Playbacks and validation:
- Post-rehearsal checklist: confirm runbook steps execute in test environment, synthetic monitor fires, alert routes to correct oncall, and incident postmortem template is triggered.
- Acceptance criteria for each pilot: metrics reported automatically, runbook validated in rehearsal, product owner sign-off recorded as Confluence comment.

Next steps (immediate action items):
- Priya: schedule weekly sync & create campaign board (ENG-1428).
- Marcus: produce dashboard query stubs for the three pilot services by 2026-11-20.
- Emma: draft customer-facing commitment language v0 and send to legal by 2026-11-22.
- Ava: draft runbook template and a sample filled runbook for hosted-api by 2026-11-24.

Appendix: sample commitment spec (template line examples)
- metric_name: p99_response_latency_route_X
- window: 30d rolling
- target: < 350ms
- consequence_description: degraded UX for interactive completions; prioritize mitigation via cache bypass and autoscale.

Notes: this doc is intentionally pragmatic and campaign-focused — not a final governance document. The purpose is to accelerate real, testable commitments and build a repeatable onboarding checklist so other services can adopt the same pattern after the pilot phase.
